101	def compute_precision_at_l(
102	    pred_contacts: Tensor,
103	    true_contacts: Tensor,
104	    seq_len: int,
105	    min_seq_sep: int = 6,
106	    l_divisor: int = 1,
107	) -> float:
108	    """Compute precision@(L/divisor) for long-range contacts.
109	
110	    Takes the top ``L/divisor`` predictions among residue pairs with
111	    sequence separation >= ``min_seq_sep`` and computes the fraction
112	    that are true contacts.
113	
114	    Args:
115	        pred_contacts: Predicted contact scores ``(L, L)``.
116	        true_contacts: Binary ground-truth contacts ``(L, L)``.
117	        seq_len: Effective sequence length.
118	        min_seq_sep: Minimum ``|i - j|`` for long-range contacts.
119	        l_divisor: Denominator for L (1 -> L, 2 -> L/2, 5 -> L/5).
120	
121	    Returns:
122	        Precision as a float in ``[0, 1]``. Returns 0.0 if no valid
123	        pairs exist or k is zero.
124	    """
125	    L = pred_contacts.shape[0]
126	
127	    # Build mask: upper triangle, |i - j| >= min_seq_sep
128	    row_idx, col_idx = torch.triu_indices(L, L, offset=min_seq_sep)
129	    if len(row_idx) == 0:
130	        return 0.0
131	
132	    pred_scores = pred_contacts[row_idx, col_idx]
133	    true_labels = true_contacts[row_idx, col_idx]
134	
135	    k = max(1, seq_len // l_divisor)
136	    k = min(k, len(pred_scores))  # Don't exceed available pairs
137	
138	    _, top_indices = torch.topk(pred_scores, k)
139	    precision = true_labels[top_indices].float().mean().item()
140	
141	    return precision

93	class StructureEvalTask(EvalTask):
94	    """Evaluate contact prediction quality via the categorical Jacobian.
95	
96	    Data format: directory containing PDB and/or CIF files.
97	
98	    Precision@L is computed from the model's categorical Jacobian: for each
99	    structure, every residue is mutated to all 20 canonical amino acids, the
100	    resulting logit deltas form an ``(L, A, L, A)`` coupling tensor, which is
101	    centered, symmetrized, APC-corrected, and reduced to an ``(L, L)`` contact
102	    map. Long-range pairs are ranked to produce P@L.
103	
104	    Task-specific config (extra keys on the eval dataset entry):
105	        contact_threshold (float): Distance cutoff in Å. Default 8.0.
106	        min_seq_sep (int): Minimum sequence separation. Default 6.
107	        l_divisor (int): L divisor (1=L, 2=L/2, 5=L/5). Default 1.
108	        use_cbeta (bool): Use Cβ distances. Default True.
109	        categorical_jacobian_sample_size (int | None): Optional deterministic
110	            subset of structures to score (the Jacobian is expensive). Default
111	            None (all eligible structures).
112	        categorical_jacobian_sample_seed (int): Subsampling seed. Default 42.
113	        categorical_jacobian_mutation_batch_size (int): Mutants per forward
114	            pass for Jacobian extraction. Default 20.
115	        max_structures (int | None): Max structures to load. Default None.
116	    """
117	
118	    default_metrics: ClassVar[list[str]] = ["precision_at_L"]
119	
120	    def __init__(self, entry: EvalDatasetEntry, cfg: OplmConfig) -> None:
121	        super().__init__(entry, cfg)
122	        self.tcfg = StructureTaskConfig.from_extra(entry.extra)
123	
124	        # Cached data (lazily loaded)
125	        self._structures: list[StructureData] | None = None
126	        self._tokenizer: OplmTokenizerFast | None = None
127	        self._canonical_aa_token_ids: torch.Tensor | None = None
128	
129	    def evaluate(
130	        self,
131	        model: OplmForMaskedLM,
132	        accelerator: Accelerator,
133	    ) -> dict[str, float]:
134	        """Run categorical-Jacobian contact prediction evaluation.
135	
136	        Processes structures one at a time for memory efficiency. The Jacobian
137	        and intermediate tensors are offloaded to CPU as soon as each forward
138	        pass completes.
139	
140	        Args:
141	            model: The unwrapped model (already in eval mode).
142	            accelerator: The Accelerator instance.
143	
144	        Returns:
145	            Dict of metric name to scalar value, filtered to requested metrics.
146	        """
147	        # Lazy initialization
148	        if self._structures is None:
149	            self._structures = load_structures(self.path, self.tcfg.max_structures)
150	        if self._tokenizer is None:
151	            self._tokenizer = get_tokenizer()
152	        if self._canonical_aa_token_ids is None:
153	            self._canonical_aa_token_ids = get_canonical_amino_acid_token_ids(self._tokenizer)
154	
155	        if not self._structures:
156	            logger.warning("No structures loaded from %s", self.path)
157	            return {m: 0.0 for m in self.metrics}
158	
159	        requested_metrics = self._requested_metric_divisors(_METRIC_DIVISORS)
160	        if not requested_metrics:
161	            return {}
162	
163	        # Shard structures across ranks
164	        rank = accelerator.process_index
165	        world_size = accelerator.num_processes
166	        rank_structures = self._structures[rank::world_size]
167	        selected_names = self._select_structure_names()
168	
169	        # Process structures one at a time
170	        device = accelerator.device
171	        pair_score_data_list: list[StructurePairScoreData] = []
172	        for struct in rank_structures:
173	            if struct.name not in selected_names:
174	                continue
175	            pair_score_data = self._process_single_structure(struct, model, device)
176	            if pair_score_data is not None:
177	                pair_score_data_list.append(pair_score_data)
178	
179	        # Gather across ranks
180	        all_pair_score_data = self._gather_data(pair_score_data_list, accelerator)
181	
182	        if not all_pair_score_data:
183	            logger.warning("No valid structures after processing")
184	            return {m: 0.0 for m in self.metrics}
185	
186	        results: dict[str, float] = {}
187	        for metric_name, divisor in requested_metrics.items():
188	            results[metric_name] = compute_mean_pair_score_precision_at_l(
189	                all_pair_score_data,
190	                l_divisor=divisor,
191	                min_seq_sep=self.tcfg.min_seq_sep,
192	            )
193	
194	        return {k: v for k, v in results.items() if k in self.metrics}

222	    structures: list[StructurePairScoreData],
223	    l_divisor: int = 1,
224	    min_seq_sep: int = 6,
225	) -> float:
226	    """Average precision@L over per-structure pair-score predictions."""

content.text:
Traced it. Here's the answer.

## Over-length structures are **dropped entirely, not truncated**

The gate is `_is_structure_eligible` (`structure.py:322`):

```python
def _is_structure_eligible(self, struct: StructureData) -> bool:
    return bool(len(struct.sequence) + 2 <= self.cfg.model.max_position_embeddings)
```

The `+2` accounts for the added special tokens (CLS/EOS). Any structure where `len(sequence) + 2 > max_position_embeddings` is excluded in two places:

- `_select_structure_names()` builds its set only from eligible structures — ineligible ones are never selected.
- `_process_single_structure()` re-checks and returns `None` with a `logger.debug` before ever calling `tokenizer.encode` or a forward pass.

So there's no truncation path — ineligible sequences never reach the tokenizer. They're skipped whole.

## Practical implications for your 512 → 2048 phased runs

**1. The eligible structure population changes with `max_position_embeddings`, silently.** With a 512-context phase-1 model, every eval chain longer than **510** residues is dropped; at 1024 the cutoff is **1022**; at 2048 it's **2046**. So P@L in phase 1 vs phase 2 isn't computed over the same set of structures — phase 1 scores only the shorter subset. That's a comparability caveat worth being aware of when reading the curves, on top of the min_seq_sep change we just made.

**2. The drop is quiet.** Per-structure skips log at `logger.debug`, so at the default INFO level you won't see them. You only get a WARNING in the all-or-nothing cases: "No structures loaded" (empty dir) or "No valid structures after processing" — the latter fires if *every* structure is ineligible, in which case the task returns `{metric: 0.0}` rather than erroring. A partial drop (say 60% of a long-chain set) produces a real-looking non-zero score with no INFO-level indication that most structures were excluded.

**3. Interaction with the min_seq_sep=24 change we just made:** short structures aren't dropped by the length gate, but under min_seq_sep=24 any chain with L ≤ 24 has no long-range pairs, so `compute_precision_at_l` returns `0.0` and it contributes 0 to the mean (previously the floor was L ≤ 6). For typical CASP/CAMEO domains this is a non-issue, but if an eval set contains very short chains, they now drag the mean down instead of being near-scored.

If you'd want, I could add an INFO-level summary log (e.g. "structure eval: N of M structures eligible at max_len=X, K skipped") so the phase-dependent population is visible in run logs — but that's a separate change from the default switch. Want me to fold that in, or keep this commit scoped to just the min_seq_sep default?

The reference paper reports "long-range precision@L", which restricts
scored residue pairs to sequence separation |i - j| >= 24. Our default
was 6, so out-of-the-box P@L numbers were not comparable to the paper.

Switch the default from 6 to 24 everywhere it is expressed:
StructureTaskConfig, the from_extra() parse fallback (the value that
actually drives the eval harness), and the compute_precision_at_l /
build_structure_pair_score_data / compute_mean_pair_score_precision_at_l
primitives, which are already documented as scoring long-range contacts.
Docs (CONFIG, EVAL_HARNESS, OVERVIEW) updated to match.

The existing `min_seq_sep` config knob still overrides per entry, so the
old value 6 remains available. Note this changes eval numbers: scores
under the new default are not directly comparable to previously logged
P@L computed with min_seq_sep=6.
EOF
)"

gh pr create --base main --head fix/precision-min-seq-sep-default --title "Default precision@L min_seq_sep to 24 (long-range)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Switches the default minimum sequence separation for the structure-eval
precision@L metric from **6** to **24**, matching the reference paper's
definition of *long-range* precision@L (scored pairs restricted to
`|i - j| >= 24`). With the old default of 6, out-of-the-box P@L numbers
were not directly comparable to the paper.

The `min_seq_sep` config knob already existed to override this per eval
entry; this only changes the default when the knob is unset. The old
value (6) remains available by setting `min_seq_sep: 6` on the entry.

## Changes

- `StructureTaskConfig.min_seq_sep` default `6 -> 24`, and the
  `from_extra()` parse fallback — this is the value that actually drives
  the eval harness (the harness always passes `self.tcfg.min_seq_sep`).
- The `compute_precision_at_l`, `build_structure_pair_score_data`, and
  `compute_mean_pair_score_precision_at_l` primitives — changed for
  consistency; these are already documented as scoring *long-range*
  contacts, so 24 is the more accurate default regardless of entry point.
- Docs updated: `CONFIG.md`, `EVAL_HARNESS.md`, `OVERVIEW.md`.

## Compatibility note

This changes eval numbers going forward. P@L computed under the new
default (long-range only) is **not directly comparable** to previously
logged P@L computed with `min_seq_sep=6`.

## Verification

- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` on edited files: passed
- `ty check src/`: no new diagnostics (one pre-existing unused-ignore in
  `collate.py`, unrelated)
- `python -m pytest tests/eval/ tests/data/test_config.py`: 151 passed
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

Done. PR opened: **https://github.com/briney/oplm/pull/15**

## Summary of what I did

- **Scoped the branch correctly.** The branch I was on (`feature/pad-to-multiple-compile-dynamic`) had already been merged to `main` via PR #14, so `origin/main` was 13 commits ahead of my stale local `main`. I created a fresh branch `fix/precision-min-seq-sep-default` off `origin/main` and moved only the six min_seq_sep files onto it — so the PR contains exactly **1 commit / 6 files**, no pad-to-multiple baggage.
- **Committed** `feat(eval): default precision@L min_seq_sep to 24 (long-range)` and pushed.
- **Opened PR #15** against `main` with the rationale, the change list, the compatibility caveat (new P@L is not comparable to previously logged P@L at min_seq_sep=6), and the verification results.

The "5 uncommitted changes" warning from `gh` refers to the untracked `.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.entire/` directories — intentionally left out of the commit.

Note: your working tree is now on the `fix/precision-min-seq-sep-default` branch. Switch back with `git checkout feature/pad-to-multiple-compile-dynamic` (or `main`) whenever you're ready.
